panels.title: Validation results: one row per target (latest run by default)
panels.description: Precision = Matching alerts / Total alerts. A ZAP alert matches when its CWE is in the app's known vulnerability list (configs/ground_truth.json). Recall = Known types detected / Known types. 'Coverage too low' means fewer than the minimum number of pages was reached (configs/validation.json).

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.target AS "Target", r.known_vulns AS "Known types", r.detected AS "Detected types", r.matching_alerts AS "Matching alerts", r.total_alerts AS "Total alerts", CASE WHEN r.coverage_ok THEN round(r.precision::numeric, 3)::text ELSE 'Coverage too low' END AS "Precision", CASE WHEN r.coverage_ok THEN round(r.recall::numeric, 3)::text ELSE 'Coverage too low' END AS "Recall", r.run_time AS "Run time" FROM validation_results r WHERE (('$run_date' = 'latest' AND r.id IN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (target) id FROM validation_results ORDER BY target, run_date DESC, id DESC)) OR ('$run_date' <> 'latest' AND r.run_date::text = '$run_date')) ORDER BY r.target

options.content:
**Precision is low because most ZAP alerts are informational, not because the scanner is wrong.** Most ZAP alerts are informational: missing security headers, cookie flags, version leaks. They are real observations but do not map to a known vulnerability type, so they count against precision. Recall is the number that matters for detection.

**Per-category recall** is 1 (detected) or 0 (missed) per category, because each app lists one known class per category. A blank or 'Coverage too low' value means the run reached too few pages to judge; it is never shown as 0.

**Run date** selects an older run. 'latest' shows the most recent run for each target.

panels.title: Recall by category (latest run per target)

targets.rawSql: SELECT c.target AS "Target", c.category AS "Category", CASE WHEN c.detected IS NULL THEN 'Coverage too low' WHEN c.detected THEN 'Detected' ELSE 'Missed' END AS "Recall per category" FROM validation_categories c WHERE (('$run_date' = 'latest' AND (c.target, c.run_date) IN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (target) target, run_date FROM validation_results ORDER BY target, run_date DESC, id DESC)) OR ('$run_date' <> 'latest' AND c.run_date::text = '$run_date')) ORDER BY c.target, c.category

panels.title: Recall by target (blank = coverage too low)

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.target AS target, CASE WHEN r.coverage_ok THEN r.recall ELSE NULL END AS recall FROM validation_results r WHERE (('$run_date' = 'latest' AND r.id IN (SELECT DISTINCT ON (target) id FROM validation_results ORDER BY target, run_date DESC, id DESC)) OR ('$run_date' <> 'latest' AND r.run_date::text = '$run_date')) ORDER BY r.target

list.name: run_date
list.label: Run date
list.query: SELECT v AS __value, v AS __text FROM (SELECT 'latest' AS v, 0 AS o UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT run_date::text AS v, 1 AS o FROM validation_results) s ORDER BY o, v DESC
list.definition: latest per target, then each run date
